a: Build privacy into systems from the start, not as a retrofit only.
Know what personal data you store, why, where, and who can access it.
Use data only for disclosed purposes.
Anonymization irreversibly removes identity; pseudonymization replaces identifiers but may be reversible.
Processes to access, correct, or delete personal data on request.
Delete or aggregate data when the retention period ends.
Vendor contracts must cover security and permitted processing.
Assess risks when launching high-impact data processing.
Avoid logging secrets and raw PII; mask when needed for debug.
Store evidence of consent and make withdrawal practical.
